items.title: Charles "Creole Charlie" Levy Interview, 1962-01-03
items.q: The interviewee does not mention Munez; the interviewer suggests 'Munez might have been' part of the band, and the interviewee confirms the band's existence but does not claim personal interaction with Munez.

ctx.x: I think he was right on the corner, right on the, what's that, Pete Lalo? Yes. I remember him and then. Corner place near the station, huh? Yeah, it was, what was it, Iperville Street? It was where the district was. I wasn't supposed to be there, but I sneaked in. And I had two three kids. One of them was studying saxophone, a couple of them studying violin, and one was studying bass. We were all interested, crazy about music, you know. And oh yeah, we used to go down the, halfway down the stairs there, they did…

Well, yeah, La Rocca and Shields. Yeah, Shields, yes. And Munez might have been. Munez, yeah, yes it was. Yeah, Yellow Munez. There was a fellow by the name of Gussie, Gussie, what was his name, was the trombone for a while. And the piano player was Ragus. Yes, that's right. Now, those fellows, when they came north, shifted around a little bit. They did, they had a choral.

They had a choral, they had a choral. I know it. You know, I know Tony Ladder very well. Tony Ladder was the drummer that followed the first drummer they had. I know him very well, and he told me quite a bit about it, and I was telling him, he laughed, and I told him how his kids used to walk down the stairs, and I think, pretty sure it was Gunn-Raw's Cave, and listened to that music, and it was so entrancing, it had so much to it, I gave.
